commands.description: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: import-memory
commands.description: Import a memory export from another AI assistant into Claude's memory — conversationally, additively, and with the content treated as data. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: morning
commands.description: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: pdf
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: pptx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: skill-creator
commands.description: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: xlsx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved. (claude.ai sync)

# Playthrough Strategy

Pre-made strategy for the agent, plus the agent's own notes added as it plays. Every chapter has
its own section below with a **Recruits** table (pre-filled by the human) and an **Agent notes**
area (filled in by the agent). Broad, cross-chapter lessons go under **Broad strategy notes**.

## General Strategy

- Always select "yes" to accept side missions when offered the choice to do so.
- Once Merlinus has joined your party, you will be prompted at the beginning of every single chapter whether or not you want to deploy him. Always select yes.

## Recruiting Units

In each chapter, there are often units that appear as green units (uncontrollable allies) or red units (enemies). These units can often be recruited by executing the Talk action with a specific player-controlled unit, but there are some more complex conditions that have to be fulfilled in order to recruit some characters. For each chapter, you have been provided a list of the recruitable units that appear and the conditions that need to be fulfilled in order to recruit the character. You should try to recruit units if possible, but it is not a strict requirement.

The chapter sections below cover Lyn mode and Hector mode. Eliwood mode is not covered. Recruits are the same on normal and hard difficulty throughout the entire game, so use the list for your mode regardless of difficulty.

## Broad strategy notes

Cross-chapter lessons the agent adds as it plays. Append below.

- Re-run `fe7_threat` AFTER moving units, not just before: a tile a unit vacates opens a path. On Ch.13, Rebecca stepped from (15,5) to a "safe" (15,4) and a pegasus took the tile she left. Also forecast EVERY attack, even "sure" finishes: a 3-HP cavalier standing in a forest made Eliwood's attack 68%, and he ate 10 damage.
- Blocking works: enemies (fliers included) cannot path through your units. Surround a fragile lord's open tiles so at most one melee attacker can reach anyone. Marcus on a fort and Oswin (Def 13) make excellent bait.
- RAIN (Ch.14): your units' plain costs double (mounted units pay 3), but `fe7_threat` ignores weather, and on Ch.14 enemy fliers and pirates still moved their full range. Trust the threat map, not "the rain slows them too". Pirates walk on river and sea tiles. (s02)
- Counters use the EQUIPPED weapon (slot 0). Before using a unit as bait, equip its cheap weapon with a forecast plus `weapon_slot`, or it will burn Javelin or Silver uses. `fe7_wait`'s A/Start presses can run straight through the post-chapter save prompt AND the next chapter's Preparations. (s02)
- Enemy fighters break "Wall" tiles with the second wall ID (1B in `fe7_terrain`) within about two turns, and enemy mercs/thieves carry Door Keys and open doors. A "sealed" room isn't. Give a blocker a margin of 8+ HP over the worst all-hit total; a 2-HP margin lost Dorcas to a crit. Use vulneraries on the turn before they are needed, not after. (s03)
- HECTOR HAS NO WEAPON after Ch.15. With no shop or trade tool, treat him as a non-combatant tank. He still blocks well (Def 14), but he cannot counter. (s03)
- The Preparations screen has a working **Trade** menu, driven by raw presses with a screenshot after each because input lags. Use it every chapter to put weapons where they matter. **Ballistae are invisible to `fe7_threat`**: unexplained damage with no enemy weapon use is a ballista (range 3-10), so screenshot the map to find it. An enemy whose counter weapon is the equipped melee weapon cannot counter at range 2: forecast it, since free chip damage may be available. (s04)

### Chapter 13 — In Search of Truth

**Objectives:**

Seize the gate at (2,10) (bottom-left, inside a walled pen entered only from (2,11)). Boss: Lv13 Knight on the gate, Steel Lance, Def 15.

**Recruits:**

| character | starts as | recruit with / action    | important condition  |
| --------- | --------- | ------------------------ | -------------------- |
| **guy**   | enemy     | **matthew** talks to him | don't kill him first |

**Agent notes:**

- s01 (attempt 1, start): 10 deployed — Hector, Eliwood, Marcus, Rebecca, Lowen, Bartre, Oswin, Serra, Matthew, Dorcas. 19 enemies: 6 pegasi (Move 7, fly), 5 archers, 4 cavaliers, a brigand, a lance unit, Guy (Myrmidon, KILLING EDGE) at (7,14), boss.
- Guy cannot be recruited (no Talk tool) — expect him in `unrecruited`.
- River is impassable to foot/mounted units (Lords/brigands only at cost 5); the only crossing to the gate side is the bridge at (10,14)-(10,15). Route: east pass (15-17,7-8) -> south basin -> bridge -> west.
- Villages: (12,9) entered from (12,10); (1,2) in the far NW across the river.

**s01 result — WON on attempt 1, seized turn 17. No deaths. Guy not recruited (killed by Oswin T7; no Talk tool).**
- How it went: held the NE start until the east pass (17,7) was clear, then used Marcus on the fort (13,13) and Oswin as bait while everyone else sat on 0-threat tiles. Enemies came in piecemeal and died on counters. Crossed at the bridge (10,14). The boss never leaves the gate: Oswin Javelin + Hector Hand Axe chip from range 2, then Marcus Silver Lance from (2,11) (crit killed it). Pegasi died charging Marcus/Oswin.
- Both villages were razed by brigands before anyone could visit: (12,9) on T4, (1,2) around T9. To get them, send someone (12,10) by T3. Reinforcements spawn from the forts (8,15), (11,16), (12,16), (0,13) through about T7.
- Level-ups: Hector 7, Eliwood 2, Marcus 2, Rebecca 2, Oswin 10, Serra 4, Dorcas 7. All at full HP at handover.
- Weapon uses: Hector Hand Axe 6 / Wolf Beil 9 (Wolf Beil is effective vs cavalry, 21 dmg). Marcus Silver Lance 18 / Iron Sword 18 (sword running low). Serra Heal 19. Oswin Javelin 14 / Iron Lance 33. Rebecca Iron Bow 41.
- The army has no magic: the Def 15+2 gate knight was only killable by Marcus. Expect armoured bosses to be Marcus's job until a mage joins (Erk in Ch.14).
- Save prompt after the chapter: chose Save, slot 1 (the slot already in use, "Ch.13"). 13x did not trigger; the game went straight to Ch.14 (Preparations, objective "Defeat enemy").

### Chapter 14 — False Friends

**Objectives:**

"Defeat enemy" — rout all enemies (30 at start, plus fort spawns). Rain mid-chapter. Boss Erik (Cavalier, Steel Lance).

**Recruits:**

| character     | starts as | recruit with / action                    | important condition               |
| ------------- | --------- | ---------------------------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| **erk**       | green npc | **serra or priscilla** talks to him      | —                                 |
| **priscilla** | village   | **any unit visits the southern village** | protect the village from brigands |

**Agent notes:**

**Objective:** "Defeat enemy" = rout (30 at start; pegasi and pirates spawn from the forts (22,14), (27,14), (17,16) through about T6). Boss Erik (Cavalier, Steel Lance) starts at (3,7) with the west cavalry block.

**s02 result: WON on attempt 1, rout finished on the T15 enemy phase. Rebecca died (T8). Erk and Priscilla not recruited.**
- Map: you start in the NE pocket (x≥18, y≤8), cut off by a river with two bridges: (17,1) and (20,5). One tank on (18,1) and one on (21,5) seals the pocket against ground units. Five soldiers and a knight start inside the pocket at x=27: Oswin as bait on (24,3) killed four of them on T1.
- Erk (green, (11,2)) wandered west and was killed around T3, which you can't stop without a Talk tool. Both villages ((9,2) and the Priscilla village at (6,14)) were razed by T5-6 by brigands/pirates from the far west and south, and you can't reach them in time from the NE start. Treat Priscilla as unobtainable without a fast flier.
- **Rain from about T5-T10 doubled MY units' plain costs (cavaliers paid 3), but enemy pegasi and pirates still moved their full range.** I assumed the enemies were slowed too, and Rebecca was killed by a pegasus plus a pirate that walked up the river. Pirates cross rivers and sea, so the "sealed" pocket leaks through river tiles.
- Level-ups: Hector 9, Eliwood 3, Oswin 11, Bartre 5, Dorcas 8, Lowen 4, Serra 5. Hector picked up Erik's Steel Lance (unusable by him, sitting in his inventory).
- Weapons at handover: **Hector Wolf Beil 4 / Hand Axe 5**. Marcus has only the Silver Lance (15) because his Iron Sword broke. Oswin has Iron Lance 30, Javelin 1. Serra Heal 12. Eliwood Rapier 30. Weapons are now critically short.
- Handover: the wait tool's A/Start presses ran through the ending, the save prompt (choice not seen) and Ch.15's Preparations, so **Ch.15 had already started (turn 1, player phase) when I took over again**. Nobody was re-deployed; the same 9 units are out (Rebecca gone). Everyone is near full HP.
- Next time: keep Rebecca and Serra off any tile a pegasus or pirate can reach even in rain (trust `fe7_threat`, not hand-pathing). Equip Oswin's Iron Lance before baiting so his counters don't burn the Javelin (he spent 12 Javelin uses on T1).

### Chapter 15 — Talons Alight

**Objectives:**

"Defend throne" — hold the throne at (5,2) until the end of turn 7. Hector starts on it.

**Recruits:**

None.

**Agent notes:**

- s03 (attempt 1, start): 15x17 indoor map. Throne room is x3-9, y2-6, walled. Entrances: the south mouth (4,6)-(6,6) between braces (one wall of 3 blockers), the locked doors (9,4) and (9,1), and a BREAKABLE wall at (2,3) (terrain 1B). Stairs (spawn points?) at (0-1,6), (9-10,6), (4-6,7), (1,12), (11,12), (7-9,16). Chests at (2,14), (4,14), and an enemy thief heads for them.
- Matthew, Lowen and Marcus start outside in the east pocket. Matthew can open (9,4) with his Lockpick (the `door` action works).
- 16 enemies at start: 4 nomads (one is a Lv15 named one with a Longbow, range 2-3), 4 knights, 2 soldiers, 2 archers, 2 shamans, a merc and a thief.

**s03 result: WON on attempt 1. The chapter ended by itself after the turn-7 enemy phase. Dorcas died (T5 enemy phase). No recruits in this chapter.**
- The room has FOUR entrances, not one. An enemy merc with a Door Key opened (9,1) on T1, fighters broke the wall (2,3) by T3, and the south mouth needs 3 bodies. The holding pattern that worked: Hector on (9,2) (Def 14, the bows do nothing to him), Bartre on (3,3) (only one fighter can reach it, from (2,3)), and Marcus/Oswin + one more across (4,6)/(5,6)/(6,5)-(6,6). The braces (3,6), (7,6), (3,7) and (7,7) are impassable. Hector can leave the throne. Nobody ever went for it.
- Dorcas died on (6,5) at 26 HP, facing one myrmidon (doubling him) plus a shaman, with a 2-HP margin; a crit or a level difference killed him. Don't leave a blocker with a margin under about 8 HP. Kill the south shamans first: they are the only thing that hurts the wall.
- Reinforcements: fighters (hammer and hand axe) from the NW (0-1,0-3) every turn, cavaliers from (14,9)/(14,11), and swords from the south stairs.
- Level-ups: Hector 10, Eliwood 4, Bartre 7, Oswin 12. All units full HP at handover (chapter heal).
- **Weapons at handover are critical. Hector has NO usable weapon (Wolf Beil and Hand Axe both broke; he holds only an unusable Steel Lance).** Marcus Silver Lance 10. Oswin Iron Lance 21 / Javelin 1. Bartre Iron Axe 29 / Hand Axe 10. Lowen Iron Lance 31 / Iron Sword 42. Eliwood Rapier 27. Matthew Iron Sword 36. Serra Heal 6 + 2 Vulneraries. Hector's and Eliwood's vulneraries are used up.
- Handover: one Start press after the win skipped the ending straight to Ch.16 Preparations ("Seize gate"). No save prompt or title card was seen; `fe7_wait`'s presses had already cleared 8 event screens.

### Chapter 16 — Noble Lady of Caelin

**Objectives:**

"Seize gate": the gate is at (21,3) inside castle walls and can only be entered from (21,4). Boss: a Lv8 Knight with a Steel Lance and a Javelin, who never leaves the gate (Def 14 on the gate, regenerates about 3 HP a turn).

**Recruits:**

None.

**Agent notes:**

**s04 result: WON on attempt 1, seized turn 25. No deaths.** Lyn, Sain, Kent and Wil start in the SE corner; Florina starts with the main group in the NW.
- **Use the Preparations Trade menu** (raw presses; inputs lag about one screenshot behind, so screenshot after every press). I gave Bartre's Hand Axe to Hector, Hector's unusable Horseslayer to Marcus (one-shots or doubles cavaliers) and Lowen's Iron Sword to Marcus, and moved Serra's Vulnerary to Hector. The convoy was empty, with 0 gold.
- The NW start is a pocket sealed by a diagonal cliff; holding a 3-tile line at (3,8)/(4,8)/(5,8) shuts out ground units. **Cavaliers spawn at (1,0)/(3,0) INSIDE the pocket, two per turn, on turns 9-12**, then stop. Forts (15,2)/(15,4) spawned cavaliers and mercs on turns 4-5.
- **The SE archer sits on a BALLISTA at (22,9)** (and earlier near (20,8)): 16 attack at range 3-10, which `fe7_threat` does not show and which spends no weapon use. It took Lyn from 18 to 4 and Kent from 11 to 1. Stay 11+ tiles away. Cliffs at rows 9-10 seal the SE corner from the north; kill it by flying Florina onto the adjacent cliff (21,9), where neither the bow nor the ballista can answer.
- Boss: it starts with the Steel Lance equipped and does NOT counter at range 2, so javelin/bow chip is free until it attacks someone with its javelin on its own phase. After that the javelin is equipped and it counters at range 1-2 (21 attack). Marcus at full HP (fort-healed 6/turn from 1 HP) with the Silver Lance (15×2) killed it; Hector then walked through allies onto (21,3).
- Level-ups: Hector 11, Florina 11, Bartre 8, Kent 5, Lowen 5, Lyn 4, Wil 7, Serra 6, Marcus +1.
- **Weapons at handover are critical:** Hector has NO weapon (Hand Axe broke; one Vulnerary). Serra's Heal broke, so there is **no healer**. Marcus has Silver ~8, Horseslayer 1, Iron Sword 34. Oswin has Iron Lance 15 and possibly 1 Javelin. Florina has Javelin ~16, Slim Lance 5, and a Fire tome she can't use. Bartre Iron Axe 23, Lowen Iron Lance 26, Eliwood Rapier ~25, Lyn Mani Katti 42 + 1 Vulnerary, Sain Iron Lance 37, Kent Iron Sword 45, Wil Iron Bow 41, Matthew Iron Sword 35.
- Ending: one Save prompt; I chose slot 3, the highlighted slot already holding the latest progress ("Ch.16"). Merlinus spoke over Ch.17 Preparations and one A press passed it with no Yes/No seen, and Merlinus is not in the deployed list. The next session should check Pick Units. Ch.17 is "Seize throne".

# Playthrough Strategy

Pre-made strategy for the agent, plus the agent's own notes added as it plays. Every chapter has
its own section below with a **Recruits** table (pre-filled by the human) and an **Agent notes**
area (filled in by the agent). Broad, cross-chapter lessons go under **Broad strategy notes**.

## General Strategy

- Always select "yes" to accept side missions when offered the choice to do so.
- Once Merlinus has joined your party, you will be prompted at the beginning of every single chapter whether or not you want to deploy him. Always select yes.

## Recruiting Units

In each chapter, there are often units that appear as green units (uncontrollable allies) or red units (enemies). These units can often be recruited by executing the Talk action with a specific player-controlled unit, but there are some more complex conditions that have to be fulfilled in order to recruit some characters. For each chapter, you have been provided a list of the recruitable units that appear and the conditions that need to be fulfilled in order to recruit the character. You should try to recruit units if possible, but it is not a strict requirement.

The chapter sections below cover Lyn mode and Hector mode. Eliwood mode is not covered. Recruits are the same on normal and hard difficulty throughout the entire game, so use the list for your mode regardless of difficulty.

## Broad strategy notes

Cross-chapter lessons the agent adds as it plays. Append below.

- Re-run `fe7_threat` AFTER moving units, not just before: a tile a unit vacates opens a path. On Ch.13, Rebecca stepped from (15,5) to a "safe" (15,4) and a pegasus took the tile she left. Also forecast EVERY attack, even "sure" finishes: a 3-HP cavalier standing in a forest made Eliwood's attack 68%, and he ate 10 damage.
- Blocking works: enemies (fliers included) cannot path through your units. Surround a fragile lord's open tiles so at most one melee attacker can reach anyone. Marcus on a fort and Oswin (Def 13) make excellent bait.
- RAIN (Ch.14): your units' plain costs double (mounted units pay 3), but `fe7_threat` ignores weather, and on Ch.14 enemy fliers and pirates still moved their full range. Trust the threat map, not "the rain slows them too". Pirates walk on river and sea tiles. (s02)
- Counters use the EQUIPPED weapon (slot 0). Before using a unit as bait, equip its cheap weapon with a forecast plus `weapon_slot`, or it will burn Javelin or Silver uses. `fe7_wait`'s A/Start presses can run straight through the post-chapter save prompt AND the next chapter's Preparations. (s02)
- Enemy fighters break "Wall" tiles with the second wall ID (1B in `fe7_terrain`) within about two turns, and enemy mercs/thieves carry Door Keys and open doors. A "sealed" room isn't. Give a blocker a margin of 8+ HP over the worst all-hit total; a 2-HP margin lost Dorcas to a crit. Use vulneraries on the turn before they are needed, not after. (s03)
- HECTOR HAS NO WEAPON after Ch.15. With no shop or trade tool, treat him as a non-combatant tank. He still blocks well (Def 14), but he cannot counter. (s03)
- The Preparations screen has a working **Trade** menu, driven by raw presses with a screenshot after each because input lags. Use it every chapter to put weapons where they matter. **Ballistae are invisible to `fe7_threat`**: unexplained damage with no enemy weapon use is a ballista (range 3-10), so screenshot the map to find it. An enemy whose counter weapon is the equipped melee weapon cannot counter at range 2: forecast it, since free chip damage may be available. (s04)

**Agent notes:**

- s01 (attempt 1, start): 10 deployed — Hector, Eliwood, Marcus, Rebecca, Lowen, Bartre, Oswin, Serra, Matthew, Dorcas. 19 enemies: 6 pegasi (Move 7, fly), 5 archers, 4 cavaliers, a brigand, a lance unit, Guy (Myrmidon, KILLING EDGE) at (7,14), boss.
- Guy cannot be recruited (no Talk tool) — expect him in `unrecruited`.
- River is impassable to foot/mounted units (Lords/brigands only at cost 5); the only crossing to the gate side is the bridge at (10,14)-(10,15). Route: east pass (15-17,7-8) -> south basin -> bridge -> west.
- Villages: (12,9) entered from (12,10); (1,2) in the far NW across the river.

**s01 result — WON on attempt 1, seized turn 17. No deaths. Guy not recruited (killed by Oswin T7; no Talk tool).**
- How it went: held the NE start until the east pass (17,7) was clear, then used Marcus on the fort (13,13) and Oswin as bait while everyone else sat on 0-threat tiles. Enemies came in piecemeal and died on counters. Crossed at the bridge (10,14). The boss never leaves the gate: Oswin Javelin + Hector Hand Axe chip from range 2, then Marcus Silver Lance from (2,11) (crit killed it). Pegasi died charging Marcus/Oswin.
- Both villages were razed by brigands before anyone could visit: (12,9) on T4, (1,2) around T9. To get them, send someone (12,10) by T3. Reinforcements spawn from the forts (8,15), (11,16), (12,16), (0,13) through about T7.
- Level-ups: Hector 7, Eliwood 2, Marcus 2, Rebecca 2, Oswin 10, Serra 4, Dorcas 7. All at full HP at handover.
- Weapon uses: Hector Hand Axe 6 / Wolf Beil 9 (Wolf Beil is effective vs cavalry, 21 dmg). Marcus Silver Lance 18 / Iron Sword 18 (sword running low). Serra Heal 19. Oswin Javelin 14 / Iron Lance 33. Rebecca Iron Bow 41.
- The army has no magic: the Def 15+2 gate knight was only killable by Marcus. Expect armoured bosses to be Marcus's job until a mage joins (Erk in Ch.14).
- Save prompt after the chapter: chose Save, slot 1 (the slot already in use, "Ch.13"). 13x did not trigger; the game went straight to Ch.14 (Preparations, objective "Defeat enemy").

### Chapter 14 — False Friends

**Objectives:**

"Defeat enemy" — rout all enemies (30 at start, plus fort spawns). Rain mid-chapter. Boss Erik (Cavalier, Steel Lance).

**Recruits:**

| character     | starts as | recruit with / action                    | important condition               |
| ------------- | --------- | ---------------------------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| **erk**       | green npc | **serra or priscilla** talks to him      | —                                 |

**Agent notes:**

**Objective:** "Defeat enemy" = rout (30 at start; pegasi and pirates spawn from the forts (22,14), (27,14), (17,16) through about T6). Boss Erik (Cavalier, Steel Lance) starts at (3,7) with the west cavalry block.

**s02 result: WON on attempt 1, rout finished on the T15 enemy phase. Rebecca died (T8). Erk and Priscilla not recruited.**
- Map: you start in the NE pocket (x≥18, y≤8), cut off by a river with two bridges: (17,1) and (20,5). One tank on (18,1) and one on (21,5) seals the pocket against ground units. Five soldiers and a knight start inside the pocket at x=27: Oswin as bait on (24,3) killed four of them on T1.
- Erk (green, (11,2)) wandered west and was killed around T3, which you can't stop without a Talk tool. Both villages ((9,2) and the Priscilla village at (6,14)) were razed by T5-6 by brigands/pirates from the far west and south, and you can't reach them in time from the NE start. Treat Priscilla as unobtainable without a fast flier.
- **Rain from about T5-T10 doubled MY units' plain costs (cavaliers paid 3), but enemy pegasi and pirates still moved their full range.** I assumed the enemies were slowed too, and Rebecca was killed by a pegasus plus a pirate that walked up the river. Pirates cross rivers and sea, so the "sealed" pocket leaks through river tiles.
- Level-ups: Hector 9, Eliwood 3, Oswin 11, Bartre 5, Dorcas 8, Lowen 4, Serra 5. Hector picked up Erik's Steel Lance (unusable by him, sitting in his inventory).
- Weapons at handover: **Hector Wolf Beil 4 / Hand Axe 5**. Marcus has only the Silver Lance (15) because his Iron Sword broke. Oswin has Iron Lance 30, Javelin 1. Serra Heal 12. Eliwood Rapier 30. Weapons are now critically short.
- Handover: the wait tool's A/Start presses ran through the ending, the save prompt (choice not seen) and Ch.15's Preparations, so **Ch.15 had already started (turn 1, player phase) when I took over again**. Nobody was re-deployed; the same 9 units are out (Rebecca gone). Everyone is near full HP.
- Next time: keep Rebecca and Serra off any tile a pegasus or pirate can reach even in rain (trust `fe7_threat`, not hand-pathing). Equip Oswin's Iron Lance before baiting so his counters don't burn the Javelin (he spent 12 Javelin uses on T1).

### Chapter 15 — Talons Alight

**Objectives:**

"Defend throne" — hold the throne at (5,2) until the end of turn 7. Hector starts on it.

**Recruits:**

None.

**Agent notes:**

- s03 (attempt 1, start): 15x17 indoor map. Throne room is x3-9, y2-6, walled. Entrances: the south mouth (4,6)-(6,6) between braces (one wall of 3 blockers), the locked doors (9,4) and (9,1), and a BREAKABLE wall at (2,3) (terrain 1B). Stairs (spawn points?) at (0-1,6), (9-10,6), (4-6,7), (1,12), (11,12), (7-9,16). Chests at (2,14), (4,14), and an enemy thief heads for them.
- Matthew, Lowen and Marcus start outside in the east pocket. Matthew can open (9,4) with his Lockpick (the `door` action works).
- 16 enemies at start: 4 nomads (one is a Lv15 named one with a Longbow, range 2-3), 4 knights, 2 soldiers, 2 archers, 2 shamans, a merc and a thief.

**s03 result: WON on attempt 1. The chapter ended by itself after the turn-7 enemy phase. Dorcas died (T5 enemy phase). No recruits in this chapter.**

lines: +**s05 attempt 1: abandoned on T16 via Suspend → Restart Chapter, with Kent dead.** By then the army had no path to a win: Eliwood, Marcus and Sain were at 1 HP, Bartre and Lowen at 3, Oswin at 5, and no healing exists on this map. **Read this before playing.**

+- Map: indoor castle, 17x28. You start on a plain (rows 26-27). The only way in is a 3-wide stair at (10-12,23-25), leading to a room (rows 17-23) whose north exit is (10-12,16). From there the route to the throne runs: corridor rows 14-15 → stairs (0-1,13) → left column x0-1 → rows 4-5 → throne room x11-16 rows 1-5.

+- **No healing at all.** Serra has no staff (don't deploy her). Merlinus is an immobile tent and can't be selected. There are no forts. Every point of damage is permanent for the chapter, so the whole plan has to be "take no damage".

+- **Reinforcements:** a cavalier and a nomad appear at (0,26)/(0,27) on the starting plain every enemy phase from about T6 to T10, and attack from BEHIND along rows 26-27. A 2-tile wall at x=9 ((9,26)+(9,27); brace above at (9,25)) holds them, but only armoured units survive there. Archers also keep appearing at (5,8) inside the sealed archer room.

+- **Enemy waves:** T1-T4, a myrmidon, a mercenary and a knight at the stair top, plus 4 archers and a nomad in the room; they die easily to a 3-unit wall on (10,25)/(11,25)/(12,25). About T5-T6, 2 nomads, a cavalier (Steel Lance), a knight and an archer come down from (10-12,16). About T8, **Raven** (Steel Sword, Skill 13, Spd 15; doubles everyone squishy) follows them. Raven and Lucius can't be recruited without Priscilla, so kill Raven.

+- **The key to Bernard: the fighter at (0,6) (chEC) carries a HAMMER (item 0x26, DROPS).** Kill it with Hector or Bartre so an axe user holds it. Nothing else can dent Bernard on the throne (Def 16).

+- 7 archers sit in a room sealed by a door at (5,6) (x3-7, rows 7-9). They never left it in 16 turns, but they shoot over walls: avoid column x1 (rows 5-11), row 11 x3-7 and column x9 (rows 7-9). Column x0 is out of their range. The cavalier at (15,15), the knight at (4,14), the archer at (8,23) (Steel Bow, shoots through walls) and the shaman at (1,23) never moved.

+- What went wrong: I turtled at the stairs on two fronts. Every turn the third wall slot (whoever wasn't Hector or Oswin) took 10-18 from bows, and the rear pairs focus-fired Kent at (5,27). **Fix: before turn 1, use Prep Trade to give Bartre's Iron Axe to HECTOR** (Def 15; he counters everything and the bows do 0 to him) **and Florina's Javelin to OSWIN** (a range-2 counter against the bows). Then Hector and Oswin are the only units that ever stand where enemies can reach.

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

commands.name: doctor

Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: claude-api

Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

commands.name: docx

commands.name: google-workspace

commands.name: commit-push

commands.name: github-init
commands.description: Initializes the current directory as a git repo, commits everything, and pushes to a GitHub remote with the same name as the folder. Use when starting a new project that needs to be pushed to GitHub. (project)

commands.name: new-branch

commands.name: uv-init
commands.description: Creates a uv virtual environment and syncs dependencies. Use when setting up a Python project with uv for the first time or after cloning. (project)

commands.name: deep-research
commands.description: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. (dynamic workflow)

commands.name: design
commands.description: Grant or revoke Claude agent access to your Design projects

commands.name: design-sync
commands.description: Push a React design system to claude.ai/design. This runs a converter that bundles the real component code (from Storybook or a bare package) and uploads it. Use when the user runs /design-sync or says "sync my design system to Claude Design".

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Research and plan a large-scale change, then execute it in parallel across 5–30 isolated worktree agents that each open a PR.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts
commands.description: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions, skills whose frontmatter fails to parse); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop
commands.description: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace.

commands.name: schedule
commands.description: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule.

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

commands.name: built-in-browser
commands.description: Read this skill before the first step that uses the built-in browser, the browser pane inside the Claude desktop app (also called the in-app browser, the browser pane, Claude's browser, or "your own browser"), whose tools are named mcp__Claude_Browser__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser tool instead. It covers the pane's persistent sign-ins, tabs and preview_start, reading pages as text, site approvals, what the pane cannot open, and what to do when it cannot be reached. It is not for Claude in Chrome (mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: chrome-browser
commands.description: Read this skill before the first step that uses Claude in Chrome, the browser extension whose tools are named mcp__claude-in-chrome__* (also called Chrome, the browser extension, or the external browser) and which acts in the person's real Chrome with their own sign-ins; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__claude-in-chrome tool instead. It covers loading the tools in one ToolSearch call, checking the person's open tabs and working in a new tab, site permissions, GIF recordings, console logs, dialogs to avoid, and when to stop and ask. It is not for the built-in browser (mcp__Claude_Browser__* or mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: computer-use
commands.description: Read this skill before the first step of any request to do something in an app on the person's own computer (Notes, Finder, System Settings, any desktop app), to look at their screen, or for "computer use". Computer use (desktop control) lets Claude take screenshots of the person's desktop and control it with clicks, typing and scrolling through the Claude desktop app; its tools are named mcp__computer-use__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__computer_* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before computer use is turned on for a conversation there may be no such tools, only an enable__mcp__remote-devices__computer tool, which turns it on. It covers turning it on, picking the right tool, the access flow, and the safety rules for tiered apps, links and financial actions. It is not for websites, which go through Claude in Chrome or the built-in browser and their own skills. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: anthropic-skills:deep-research
commands.description: Use this skill when the user's prompt requires (1) researching a topic across multiple sources, comparing options or alternatives, analyzing trends or history, understanding markets or industries, or reviewing literature or studies and (2) synthesizing that research into a comprehensive, narrative report. If you're planning to search the web or internal knowledge bases, consider using this skill. This skill coordinates research subagents, so use it only when you have a tool for spawning subagents (the Agent or Task tool); otherwise, research the question directly. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: docs
commands.description: docs (editable docs people share and comment on; the default for any document, named as a doc or not: a document, report, proposal, resume, cover letter, letter, contract, policy, form, template, worksheet, essay, handbook, guide, how-to, cheat sheet, SOP or other writing to keep, share, collaborate on, send, submit, print or sign; a doc exports to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs, so needing a file to send, attach, upload, submit or print is no reason to pick Word, and a file nobody asked for is a doc, not Word; a plan, comparison, summary or notes asked in chat stays in chat; a pasted claude.ai artifact link may be a doc: check with docs tools first; Word or another file format named, tracked changes wanted, or a .docx to change or use as a template → that format's skill): making one → if no docs-connector instructions are in context, call its `guide` (topic.instructions) first; then create the doc (headings only, no body) before any search, file read or plan, even with files attached. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: docx
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of Microsoft Word Documents, such as 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', 'microsoft doc'. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers Claude's own dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead, even if they will email or print it. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: google-workspace
commands.description: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: import-memory
commands.description: Import a memory export from another AI assistant into Claude's memory — conversationally, additively, and with the content treated as data. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: morning
commands.description: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: pdf
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: pptx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: skill-creator
commands.description: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: xlsx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: design
commands.description: Grant or revoke Claude agent access to your Design projects

commands.name: design-sync
commands.description: Push a React design system to claude.ai/design. This runs a converter that bundles the real component code (from Storybook or a bare package) and uploads it. Use when the user runs /design-sync or says "sync my design system to Claude Design".

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Research and plan a large-scale change, then execute it in parallel across 5–30 isolated worktree agents that each open a PR.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts
commands.description: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions, skills whose frontmatter fails to parse); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop

commands.name: schedule

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

commands.name: built-in-browser
commands.description: Read this skill before the first step that uses the built-in browser, the browser pane inside the Claude desktop app (also called the in-app browser, the browser pane, Claude's browser, or "your own browser"), whose tools are named mcp__Claude_Browser__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser tool instead. It covers the pane's persistent sign-ins, tabs and preview_start, reading pages as text, site approvals, what the pane cannot open, and what to do when it cannot be reached. It is not for Claude in Chrome (mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: chrome-browser

It covers loading the tools in one ToolSearch call, checking the person's open tabs and working in a new tab, site permissions, GIF recordings, console logs, dialogs to avoid, and when to stop and ask. commands.name: computer-use
commands.description: Read this skill before the first step of any request to do something in an app on the person's own computer (Notes, Finder, System Settings, any desktop app), to look at their screen, or for "computer use". Computer use (desktop control) lets Claude take screenshots of the person's desktop and control it with clicks, typing and scrolling through the Claude desktop app; its tools are named mcp__computer-use__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__computer_* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before computer use is turned on for a conversation there may be no such tools, only an enable__mcp__remote-devices__computer tool, which turns it on. It covers turning it on, picking the right tool, the access flow, and the safety rules for tiered apps, links and financial actions. It is not for websites, which go through Claude in Chrome or the built-in browser and their own skills. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: anthropic-skills:deep-research
commands.description: Use this skill when the user's prompt requires (1) researching a topic across multiple sources, comparing options or alternatives, analyzing trends or history, understanding markets or industries, or reviewing literature or studies and (2) synthesizing that research into a comprehensive, narrative report. If you're planning to search the web or internal knowledge bases, consider using this skill. This skill coordinates research subagents, so use it only when you have a tool for spawning subagents (the Agent or Task tool); otherwise, research the question directly. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: docs
commands.description: docs (editable docs people share and comment on; the default for any document, named as a doc or not: a document, report, proposal, resume, cover letter, letter, contract, policy, form, template, worksheet, essay, handbook, guide, how-to, cheat sheet, SOP or other writing to keep, share, collaborate on, send, submit, print or sign; a doc exports to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs, so needing a file to send, attach, upload, submit or print is no reason to pick Word, and a file nobody asked for is a doc, not Word; a plan, comparison, summary or notes asked in chat stays in chat; a pasted claude.ai artifact link may be a doc: check with docs tools first; Word or another file format named, tracked changes wanted, or a .docx to change or use as a template → that format's skill): making one → if no docs-connector instructions are in context, call its `guide` (topic.instructions) first; then create the doc (headings only, no body) before any search, file read or plan, even with files attached. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: docx
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of Microsoft Word Documents, such as 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', 'microsoft doc'. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers Claude's own dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead, even if they will email or print it. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: google-workspace
commands.description: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: import-memory

commands.name: morning

commands.name: pdf
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: pptx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: skill-creator
commands.description: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: xlsx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: commit-push
commands.description: Commits all changes with a provided message and pushes to remote. Use when the user wants to commit and push their changes in one step. (project)

commands.name: github-init
commands.description: Initializes the current directory as a git repo, commits everything, and pushes to a GitHub remote with the same name as the folder. Use when starting a new project that needs to be pushed to GitHub. (project)

commands.name: new-branch
commands.description: Pulls the latest changes from origin to ensure main is up to date, then creates a new branch. Use when starting work on a new feature or fix. (project)

commands.name: uv-init
commands.description: Creates a uv virtual environment and syncs dependencies. Use when setting up a Python project with uv for the first time or after cloning. (project)

commands.name: deep-research
commands.description: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. (dynamic workflow)

commands.name: design
commands.description: Grant or revoke Claude agent access to your Design projects

commands.name: design-sync
commands.description: Push a React design system to claude.ai/design. This runs a converter that bundles the real component code (from Storybook or a bare package) and uploads it. Use when the user runs /design-sync or says "sync my design system to Claude Design".

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug

commands.name: code-review

**s05 attempt 2: restarted on T27 after a second death (Merlinus T7, Oswin T26).** The plan worked until the throne approach, so reuse it:
- Prep: Bartre's Iron Axe to Hector, Florina's Javelin swapped for Oswin's 1-use one. Deploy Hector, Eliwood, Marcus, Lowen, Oswin, Lyn, Sain, Kent, Wil, Matthew; bench Serra and Bartre. Merlinus deploys himself as an immobile tent at (15,26). **He counts as a unit and can die**: he died on T7 because I moved Kent, Lowen and Sain off the east corner without re-running `fe7_threat`, and a nomad walked into the gap.
- T1-T4: wall (10,25) Sain, (11,25) Hector, (12,25) Oswin. The swords and archers die to counters plus first strikes (bows can't counter at range 1).
- **Spawn camp:** pairs (a cavalier with 26-27 HP and a nomad with 22-23) appear at (0,26)/(0,27) at the end of the T6, T7, T8 and T9 enemy phases, then stop. Put Marcus on (1,26), Lyn on (1,27) and Wil on (2,27). Each turn, Lyn (effective Mani Katti, about 18) plus Wil's bow (about 11) kill the nomad, and Marcus's Silver Lance x2 kills the cavalier, before either acts. Cost: about 4 HP per wave on Marcus and all 8 Silver uses.
- North wave (2 nomads, a Steel Lance cavalier, a knight, an archer, then Raven on T8-9): Hector and Oswin bait it at row 21-22 with everyone else out of reach. Raven dies on their counters.
- **The Hammer worked:** walk Hector (alone, Def 15) up column x0. The fighter at (0,6) attacked him and died on his counters, so Hector got the HAMMER. With it he does 24x2 to knights and should do about 20x2 = 40 to Bernard (33 HP) on the throne.
- The archer room is open (thieves unlock (5,6) and (3,3) early) and the archers DO come out once something is within their move+2. They do 0-1 to Hector and Oswin, so let only those two engage them.
- **What killed Oswin: the mage (14,4) comes west along row 4 and does 14 to Oswin and 11 to Hector, at about 91%.** Oswin got boxed in by archers inside its range at 8 HP. Fix: deal with the mage first. Lure it with Marcus (Res 10, takes about 4) and kill it with 2-3 units in one player phase, before Hector and Oswin walk east. Keep Hector at 23+ HP for the Bernard exchange (Bernard's counter does 11). Hector's only Vulnerary is precious.

# Playthrough Strategy

Pre-made strategy for the agent, plus the agent's own notes added as it plays. Every chapter has
its own section below with a **Recruits** table (pre-filled by the human) and an **Agent notes**
area (filled in by the agent). Broad, cross-chapter lessons go under **Broad strategy notes**.

## General Strategy

- Always select "yes" to accept side missions when offered the choice to do so.
- Once Merlinus has joined your party, you will be prompted at the beginning of every single chapter whether or not you want to deploy him. Always select yes.

## Recruiting Units

In each chapter, there are often units that appear as green units (uncontrollable allies) or red units (enemies). These units can often be recruited by executing the Talk action with a specific player-controlled unit, but there are some more complex conditions that have to be fulfilled in order to recruit some characters. For each chapter, you have been provided a list of the recruitable units that appear and the conditions that need to be fulfilled in order to recruit the character. You should try to recruit units if possible, but it is not a strict requirement.

The chapter sections below cover Lyn mode and Hector mode. Eliwood mode is not covered. Recruits are the same on normal and hard difficulty throughout the entire game, so use the list for your mode regardless of difficulty.

## Broad strategy notes

Cross-chapter lessons the agent adds as it plays. Append below.

- Re-run `fe7_threat` AFTER moving units, not just before: a tile a unit vacates opens a path. On Ch.13, Rebecca stepped from (15,5) to a "safe" (15,4) and a pegasus took the tile she left. Also forecast EVERY attack, even "sure" finishes: a 3-HP cavalier standing in a forest made Eliwood's attack 68%, and he ate 10 damage.
- Blocking works: enemies (fliers included) cannot path through your units. Surround a fragile lord's open tiles so at most one melee attacker can reach anyone. Marcus on a fort and Oswin (Def 13) make excellent bait.
- RAIN (Ch.14): your units' plain costs double (mounted units pay 3), but `fe7_threat` ignores weather, and on Ch.14 enemy fliers and pirates still moved their full range. Trust the threat map, not "the rain slows them too". Pirates walk on river and sea tiles. (s02)
- Counters use the EQUIPPED weapon (slot 0). Before using a unit as bait, equip its cheap weapon with a forecast plus `weapon_slot`, or it will burn Javelin or Silver uses. `fe7_wait`'s A/Start presses can run straight through the post-chapter save prompt AND the next chapter's Preparations. (s02)
- Enemy fighters break "Wall" tiles with the second wall ID (1B in `fe7_terrain`) within about two turns, and enemy mercs/thieves carry Door Keys and open doors. A "sealed" room isn't. Give a blocker a margin of 8+ HP over the worst all-hit total; a 2-HP margin lost Dorcas to a crit. Use vulneraries on the turn before they are needed, not after. (s03)
- HECTOR HAS NO WEAPON after Ch.15. With no shop or trade tool, treat him as a non-combatant tank. He still blocks well (Def 14), but he cannot counter. (s03)
- The Preparations screen has a working **Trade** menu, driven by raw presses with a screenshot after each because input lags. Use it every chapter to put weapons where they matter. **Ballistae are invisible to `fe7_threat`**: unexplained damage with no enemy weapon use is a ballista (range 3-10), so screenshot the map to find it. An enemy whose counter weapon is the equipped melee weapon cannot counter at range 2: forecast it, since free chip damage may be available. (s04)
